title: Check if There is a Valid Path in a Grid
summary: Given an m x n grid where each cell represents a street with specific connections, determine if a valid path exists from the top-left cell to the bottom-right cell by following the streets without making any changes to them.
statement: Given an m x n grid where each cell represents a street with specific connections, determine if a valid path exists from the top-left cell to the bottom-right cell by following the streets without making any changes to them. The streets are represented as follows: - 1: connects the left cell and the right cell - 2: connects the upper cell and the lower cell - 3: connects the left cell and the lower cell - 4: connects the right cell and the lower cell - 5: connects the left cell and the upper cell - 6: connects the right cell and the upper cell The path must start at the top-left cell (0, 0) and end at the bottom-right cell (m - 1, n - 1).
constraints: Street types 1..6 have fixed openings; adjacent cells connect only when both face each other.
Determine reachability from top-left to bottom-right without rotating tiles.
hints: Map every tile type to its two opening direction vectors.
Traverse from the start through an opening only when the neighbor has the opposite opening.
Mark visited cells to avoid cycles and accept on reaching the destination.
The graph edges are exactly the mutually connected street borders, so graph reachability solves the problem.
editorial: The graph edges are exactly the mutually connected street borders, so graph reachability solves the problem.

tests.explanation: Compatible openings form a path through every turn to the bottom-right.
The start’s right opening meets a tile without a left opening, so no valid path exists.
